knownBest.source: Compiled by Erich Friedman; n=11 Found by Hans Melissen in 1997. Source expression: r = 2.631+. Printed table value: 2.631. Global optimality is the computer-assisted proof of VonEquinox's DiskCoveringSolve (pinned at 0895849): optimal covering radius r = 0.37998385311983868972…, and this problem's covered radius is R = 1/r. The proof reduces any smaller covering, through a minimal subcover and its restricted Voronoi partition, to finitely many disc triangulations, excludes each with exact rational certificates, and fixes the candidate with a local Taylor theorem and a rational Krawczyk root box. MinMax Arena replayed every certificate locally on 2026-10-02; the repository notes that independent external review is still pending. The continuous problem is solved; a nine-decimal certificate cannot attain this irrational value, and no grid-optimality claim is made.
